A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROVER study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and full appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original progress-estimation, frame-level reasoning, and video-QA experiments, alongside OpenX evaluations, ablations, and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original baseline comparisons, manual error analysis, inference-cost measurements, and context-window sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, recursive decomposition, the three-frame sliding window, ROVER prompts, and trajectory-generation procedure are unchanged. Larger context windows are evaluated as ablations rather than adopted as a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 543-video, 27-task RoboCasa-derived benchmark and the reported 1,000 videos from 50 OpenX datasets. The added analyses use existing task domains; the new description of OpenX diversity does not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds LocalConcat, which uses the three most recent frames, to the main comparisons in Figures 3, 5, and 7. Tables 7–9 additionally evaluate VideoGemini, VideoLLaMA-3, and Video-LLaVA. These substantially broaden the comparator set beyond the retained GVL, TemporalConcat, and LIV comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include manual error categorization across 100 real-world and 100 simulation videos, token and model-call measurements for 30- and 60-frame videos, and window-size comparisons using 3, 6, 9, and 12 frames. The existing benchmark sampling and evaluation protocols remain documented as before.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 introduces a systematic error-type audit, distinct from the retained 200-example validation of the LLM evaluator. Tables 12–13 add window-size sensitivity and associated error analysis, while Tables 5–6 examine computational cost. These substantially extend the existing component ablations and robustness checks.

E5.justification: The figures retain mean-and-standard-error reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. The new tables supply point estimates without changing uncertainty reporting for retained results.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, error-audit, cost, and window-sensitivity results. Table 9 reports QA accuracy of 77% for ROVER and 68% for VideoGemini; Table 12 reports correlations of 0.56, 0.52, 0.50, and 0.44 for windows of 3, 6, 9, and 12 frames. These are newly reported comparisons, not between-version performance gains. The detailed OpenX tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, geometric progress definitions, trajectory construction equations, and object-centric assumptions are unchanged. The added support for linear scaling consists of empirical measurements rather than new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about recursive reasoning, reduced hallucination, improved benchmark performance, dataset construction, and linear scaling. The additions mainly supply further supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 refines the mechanism discussion by attributing larger-window degradation primarily to perception errors and explaining how subtask decomposition still limits context. It also explicitly discusses reduced token usage despite additional model calls. These elaborate the existing context-focusing explanation and decomposition-failure limitation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies LocalConcat's three-most-recent-frame input and VideoGemini's all-frame input, and documents token and model-call usage. Existing ROVER prompts, backbone identifiers, hardware disclosure, and code/data access information remain unchanged. Detailed configurations for the added video-specific models are not provided.

R1.justification: Appendix 17 adds a brief positioning discussion of VideoLLaMA-3 and Video-LLaVA as specialized video-language models with temporal and memory mechanisms. The bibliography and the main and appendix related-work discussions otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative receives localized additions for error analysis, inference cost, extended baselines, and window sensitivity, while most existing prose remains intact. The conference footer and acknowledgements change. Appendix lettering becomes inconsistent numerical numbering with duplicated section numbers.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated tables for error categories, computational cost, extended comparisons, and window sensitivity. Figures 3, 5, and 7 are redrawn with LocalConcat series and revised legends, and Figure 6 is reformatted and relabeled. This substantially expands the presentation of evidence while retaining most appendix figures.

improvement.justification: The error audit, window-size experiments, and token/call measurements strengthen the evidence for ROVER's mechanism and efficiency, while added video-specific baselines broaden validation. These gains are qualified by sparse baseline configuration details and reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.3 extends a finding about contexts exceeding ten frames to three-frame LocalConcat, which is absent from the cited context-length plots. The revision provides useful additional evidence, but its integration limits the overall improvement.
